name_reason: Name follows the fd2_<descriptor> game-function convention and accurately reflects the logic: it paints the per-frame 'character takes damage' flash sprite/overlay for one runtime char. No Ghidra address residue. Sibling battle/animation helpers in battle.c use the same fd2_<verb>_<descriptor> form (fd2_render_mini_char_status_panel, fd2_play_figani_animation_loop, fd2_blit_indexed_sprite).
purpose: Paint a quick 'character takes damage' flash overlay onto a work buffer at the screen position appropriate for the target's team (and a chapter-24 special-case), delegating the actual paint to fd2_render_mini_char_status_panel.
logic_summary: screen_off defaults by team: runtime_char_array[char_unit_id].team == 0 (enemy) -> 0xC080 (lower-half panel, mode-13h byte offset = row 152 in a 0x140-stride buffer); else (ally/player) -> 0x05AB (upper-area panel, ~row 4). Override: if current_chapter_id == 0x18 (chapter 24) AND char_unit_id == 0x11 (story NPC Sumeti, who fights on the enemy side that chapter), force screen_off = 0xC080. Then call fd2_render_mini_char_status_panel(workspace_buf + screen_off, 0x140, char_unit_id). __CHK(0x10) frame check at entry. No return value; cyclomatic complexity 4.

params.name: workspace_buf
params.semantics: Base linear address of the offscreen mode-13h work buffer (0x140-byte row stride) the flash is painted into. Callers pass a malloc'd animation work buffer (pAnimWorkBuf1 / dst, e.g. malloc(64000)) from the special-attack / FIGANI cinematic routines. screen_off is added to this base before dispatch.
params.reason: Name accurately describes the value (the work/back buffer base address). No address residue; matches caller usage. src and Ghidra both already use workspace_buf.

params.name: char_unit_id
params.semantics: Index into the runtime character array (data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr, 0x50-byte stride). Used to read .team (offset 0x0E) for team-based positioning and compared against 0x11 for the chapter-24 override; passed through to fd2_render_mini_char_status_panel as the char to render. Callers pass caster_idx, *target_idx_buf, or target_idx_buf[i].
params.reason: Name accurately reflects usage (a runtime-char-array unit index). The 0x11 it is compared against is a meaningful domain char ID (Sumeti), not an address residue, so no part of the name needs changing. src and Ghidra both already use char_unit_id.

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effect: blits a got-hit flash frame for char_unit_id into workspace_buf at the team/chapter-selected screen offset via fd2_render_mini_char_status_panel.
